articles.title: Congress must save the Navy from becoming ‘hollow’
articles.summary: The article emphasizes the U.S. Constitution's crucial mandate for Congress to provide and maintain a Navy, a responsibility deemed more vital than ever. The author previously asserted in June 2022 that the U.S. Navy was 'broken,' signaling significant concerns about its operational readiness and the efficacy of Congressional oversight in ensuring its robust maintenance and strategic capabilities.

articles.title: op-system 0.4.0
articles.summary: The article introduces `op_system`, a software tool designed for specifying and compiling mathematical equations (ODEs, PDEs) critical for modeling complex multi-physics and multi-scale systems. It offers a domain-agnostic approach, enabling scientists and engineers to efficiently define right-hand sides (RHS) for diverse physical phenomena using YAML/JSON-friendly specifications. This innovation streamlines advanced scientific computing and simulation.

articles.title: She left IAF after 10 years to support family, then lost husband in MiG-21 crash; Supreme Court backs her reinstatement
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the reinstatement of a former Indian Air Force Short Service Commissioned woman officer. She had left service in 2013 and subsequently became a war widow. This landmark ruling underscores the legal system's role in addressing grievances and ensuring justice for defence personnel, even years after their initial departure, setting an important precedent.

articles.title: In 2023, recycled face-mask fibre was added to printable concrete; a 1% dose raised compressive strength by 41% over unreinforced concrete
articles.summary: In 2023, researchers successfully integrated recycled face-mask fibres into printable concrete, demonstrating a significant improvement in material strength. A mere 1% addition of these fibres increased the concrete's compressive strength by 41% compared to unreinforced concrete. This innovative development presents a sustainable approach to construction, enhancing material performance while effectively repurposing waste materials.

articles.title: In 2023, engineers melted discarded plastic bags into roof tiles; the lighter tiles showed test temperatures about 17°C lower than standard roof materials
articles.summary: In 2023, engineers successfully repurposed discarded plastic bags into innovative roof tiles. These lighter, eco-friendly tiles demonstrated significantly improved thermal performance, registering temperatures approximately 17°C lower than conventional roofing materials during tests. This development presents a promising sustainable solution for construction, potentially reducing building energy consumption and contributing to environmental conservation through waste repurposing.
